messages:
Maria Chen: Quick kickoff 10min sync. We're rolling a weighted canary (10% -> 50%) for the new routing-policy changes. Need a compact telemetry contract so the console can compute cohort deltas, handle weight normalization, and show automated regression signals.

Devon Patel: Runtime can emit per-request fields: cohort_label (enum), weight_bucket (int), routing_policy, model_rev, latency_ms, is_error, is_fallback, tokens, batch_size, kv_cache_hit, node_id, experiment_id, request_id. Will avoid free-form tags where possible.

Aditya Singh: Infra will supply node-level metrics to join (gpu_util_pct, queue_len, scheduling_delay_ms) and a 1s aggregation feed for dashboard heatmaps. Concern: emitting token_cost at full QPS is costly. Recommend sampled token_cost plus aggregated token spend counters.

Sara Lopez: Dashboard needs: side-by-side cohort comparison (normalized by weight), bootstrap CIs for p50/p95, region and region-by-cohort small multiples, and a stability indicator when sample counts < N. Also a toggle to show per-request samples vs aggregated rates.

Oliver Grant: For alerts, we want a composite severity: p95_delta_norm * latency_weight + error_rate_lift * error_weight + fallback_lift * fallback_weight. Suppress alerts during scheduled ramp windows or when sample count is low. Also annotate alerts with current rollout percent and experiment_id.

Devon Patel: Suggest enums to keep cardinality sane: cohort_label {BASELINE, CANARY, SHARED_TRAFFIC}, routing_policy enum, fallback_reason enum. Also an experiment_phase enum (ROLLING_UP, STABLE, ROLLING_DOWN).

Maria Chen: Good. We also need consistent bucketing for sampling so the same request_id hash deterministically falls into the sampled set across retries. Add sample_rate metadata in the stream header.

Aditya Singh: We'll implement deterministic hash sampling and emit sample_rate and sampled=true on events. We'll also export 10s counters: total_requests, errors, fallbacks, sum_latency_ms, sum_tokens per experiment_id+cohort so dashboards can compute quick aggregates without needing request tails.

Sara Lopez: UX request: console should compute effect sizes and show whether change is statistically/significant and practically meaningful (e.g., p95 > +5% and error_lift > 0.2pp). Provide a checkbox to auto-hide cohorts with <1k requests in window.

Devon Patel: Proto sketch (comments inline):
```proto
message TelemetryEvent {
  string request_id = 1;
  string experiment_id = 2;
  enum Cohort { BASELINE = 0; CANARY = 1; CONTROL = 2 }
  Cohort cohort = 3;
  int32 weight_bucket = 4; // e.g. 1..100
  string model_rev = 5;
  int32 latency_ms = 6;
  bool is_error = 7;
  bool is_fallback = 8;
  int32 batch_size = 9;
  int64 tokens = 10;
  bool sampled = 11; // true if this event carries heavy fields
  int64 token_cost_micros = 12; // only when sampled
  string node_id = 13; // for infra joins
  int32 experiment_phase = 14; // enum
}
```

Aditya Singh: Add sample_rate in stream metadata and include a periodic aggregate record: {timestamp, experiment_id, cohort, total_requests, errors, fallbacks, sum_latency_ms, sum_tokens}. That reduces query pressure for dashboard main view.

Oliver Grant: Also capture rollout_metadata: current_rollout_pct, ramp_start_ts, ramp_end_ts in the aggregates so alert logic can suppress during planned ramps.

Maria Chen: Action items:
- Devon: open telemetry proto PR with enum tables + deterministic sampling guidance by EOD Thu
- Aditya: add infra aggregate feed + sample_rate docs + node metrics mapping
- Sara: mock wireframes showing normalized diffs, CI, and stability flag by Mon
- Oliver: propose alert scoring formula and suppression rules by Mon

Maria Chen: tagging owners @Devon Patel @Aditya Singh @Sara Lopez @Oliver Grant :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Created PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/438 with initial proto and ingestion mapping

Sara Lopez: I'll add a dashboard test that injects synthetic aggregate records to validate diff calculations and suppression behavior.

Devon Patel: One more question: do we want latency histograms at runtime or just raw latency_ms per request and compute histograms downstream? I lean downstream to keep payload small.

Aditya Singh: Downstream histograms are fine. We'll emit latency_ms raw on sampled events and sums/counts in aggregates for approximate histograms.

Maria Chen: Great. If no objections I'll schedule a 30m sync Fri to review the PR + wireframes. Thanks everyone.
